why: The tables of three room kinds the owner asked for after pass 3 (docs/mechanics/DUNGEON_PASS2.md 'Next phase'): bank_vault (a code on signs in other rooms opens a vault), wishing_well (throw an item in, a gamble on its value) and bait_room (leave a bait; the NEXT run spawns a Pokemon lured by it). Read by tools/dungeon_extras.py. Control blocks come from data/dungeon_puzzles.json (the same console, button, lamp and plinth); GREED's prices from data/dungeon_greed.json. Nothing here is an authored dungeon's content: a dungeon's record names the rooms.

bank_vault.budget_why: A bank vault's chests are weighed like a vault's (GREED chest_cp) and held to the same limit KIT3 set (data/dungeon_greed.json vault_budget): all the chests together at most dollar_factor x the gathering tier open at the band's lowest badge count x the shortest dungeon's required hours. The kit's own vault does not enforce it yet (its authors have not rebalanced); a new kind starts inside it.

messages.hint: A code lock. The digits are written elsewhere.

wishing_well.ev_why: The well pays a share of the thrown item's GREED value (cp), rounded DOWN into a currency item, so the pay is at most share x value whatever is thrown: no item is worth more in the well than at the bank. The expected share of a band's table (sum of weight x share) is held at or under ev_cap, so throwing the reward back in loses more each time, and a gambler still has a 'more' tail (share 200 to 500) and a 'nothing' mass.
wishing_well.gaming_why: What cannot be gamed, and how. (1) Worthless items: the well prices a thrown item from GREED's table and refuses anything unpriced, a placeholder price (source 'unpriced': rare candy, exp candies, bamboo blocks) or under min_cp; it throws the item back out of the well. (2) Re-throwing the reward: at most `throws` per run; the expected share is under ev_cap so it loses on average; and GREED charges only a gain (pay minus thrown value, only when above 0), a ratchet that never refunds a loss, so a chain of throws is charged at least the net gain it makes. (3) Carried-in wealth: a gain is charged, not free; the clock only gets faster. (4) Stacks: the value is cp x count, so a stack of cheap items is the sum, and the pay is capped at max_count of the currency item.
wishing_well.shares_why: [weight, share in percent of the thrown value]. Weights sum to 100 (the well rolls random value 1..100). Share 0 is 'nothing'; 50 and 100 are the middling returns; 200, 300 and 500 are the 'more' (a chance of a better return than the gift).
wishing_well.ladders_why: [item, plural name] in rising GREED price (the generator reads each price from data/dungeon_greed.json). The pay is made in the dearest item whose price the pay reaches: a small win is iron, a big one a better thing ('more or better'). The first item must be cheap enough that the smallest real pay (min_cp x the smallest non-zero share) buys one.

messages.hint: Throw something of worth into the well.
messages.cheap: The well wants something of worth.

bait_room.why: BAIT is any item named here; Cobblemon's own bait (the fishing effects in data/cobblemon/spawn_bait_effects of the 1.8.0 jar) is a rod mechanic and is NOT used: only the item ids are. The species is ours: what the lure brings, by bait and band, one family a bait, never a legendary, mythical, Ultra Beast or paradox (the prize system owns those), never a dungeon prize line (data/dungeon_prize_roster.json), never one of the eight starters (docs/STATE.md, closed 2026-10-08). The owner, 2026-10-12: every berry the campaign lets a player obtain is a bait, and the berry's rarity IN THIS CAMPAIGN is the lure's: each bait names its tier and its source; the tier sets two SEPARATE rolls, shiny and alpha, so a lure can be shiny, alpha, rarely both, a unique reward rather than a standard mon. Rarer berries lure more coveted lines (the pinch berries: the traditional starters' lines). The Pokemon is spawned at the band's LOWER cap whatever it rolls (the prize's reasoning, tools/dungeon_prize.py: the level cap's ball refusal never fires; an alpha's reward is its look and size, not difficulty), wandering and catchable, in a living room of the run, and weighs on the clock as an ambient catch (a heavier weight for a shiny or alpha catch is proposed, not built: docs/mechanics/DUNGEON_BAIT.md 4). ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING: dg.bait stores the bait's 1-based index in this list, so the first six keep the places they had before 2026-10-12 and every new bait is appended; reordering would turn a bait a player already laid into a different Pokemon. Design: docs/mechanics/DUNGEON_BAIT.md.

common.why: The seven staple berries and the poke bait. Each staple is dropped by 18 to 27 species we spawn (docs/research/notes/drops-1.8.0.json items, droppers marked live, counted by hand), Oran and Pecha are also handed out in data/rewards.json caches, and a berry is what you plant (docs/research/notes/mint-seeds.md:110, VERIFIED) so one becomes a tree: the bait a player has from the first routes. Shiny 1%: about 20x the world's 1/2048 (modpack/config/cobblemon/main.json shinyRate 2048), a jackpot that still comes about once in a hundred lures. Alpha 5%: one lure in twenty is the big one. Both (independent rolls) 0.05%.

uncommon.why: Dropped by fewer species, or bought, or handed out a few times: the five flavour berries (11 to 15 live droppers, no cache, no shop), the 18 type-resist berries (11 to 25 live droppers at 2.5 to 10% a pass, plus a wild alpha's type reward and some dungeon vault chests), the six EV-lowering berries ($300 each from two badges, data/traders.json), Sitrus and Lum (no dropper; five caches and one) and the poke snack. Getting one is a decision and a trip, not luck. Shiny 2%, alpha 8%, both 0.16%.

rare.why: Mutation only: no dropper in drops-1.8.0.json, no shop, no cache or quest anywhere in data/. A player needs both parents planted side by side and a mutation roll on a growth (125/1000, x4 with Surprise Mulch: mint-seeds.md:115, ASSUMED there). Mago, Magost and Watmel are steps 1 to 3 of the Custap chain (docs/research/DROPS_AUDIT.md:432, read in the jar); the other cultivars' parents were not read here. Shiny 4%, alpha 12%, both 0.48%.

very_rare.why: The pinch and battle berries, mutation only. Custap is four mutation steps from five drops (DROPS_AUDIT.md:432); the other thirteen chains were not read here and are ASSUMED at least as deep (DUNGEON_BAIT.md 5, open question 1). Growing one is a farm built over many sessions; the lure pays it with a traditional starter's line and the best odds: shiny 8% (about 160x the world), alpha 20%, both 1.6%.
